name: @media-router/plugin-mpegts-demuxer
description: MPEG-TS demuxer — splits a multi-program transport stream into separate video/audio outputs

mediaRouter.description: Receives one muxed/mpegts stream and splits it into N video and M audio outputs, each on its own multicast group.

queueLeaky.description: Output-branch queue behaviour. OFF (non-leaky): never drop — bursts back-pressure into the socket buffer and the re-mux stays lossless (contribution/stability). ON (leaky): shed the oldest frame once Queue depth of backlog builds — never hold backlog (live production). The paced audio branch always stays non-leaky ahead of clocksync (a leaky queue there shears every paced burst). Queues sit after the codec parser, upstream of the branch muxer — drops always land on whole frames; the mux output is never queued.

queueDepthMs.description: Output-branch queue bound. Non-leaky: runaway safety cap (the branch normally sits near-empty). Leaky: backlog tolerance before shedding. Paced audio uses at least pacing offset + 240 ms regardless.

audioPacing.description: Pace demuxed audio to real-time frame cadence. Sources pack multiple audio frames per PES, so tsdemux releases audio in line-rate bursts that downstream decoders and SRT links hear as choppy audio; pacing restores one-frame (21 ms) cadence at the cost of the pacing offset in extra delay on audio outputs. Turn OFF for latency-critical live production where occasional burst-induced drops are preferable to added delay.

audioPacingMs.description: Audio pacing offset — must cover one source PES worth of audio (this source: ~150 ms = 7 AAC frames). Smaller-PES sources can run lower for less egress delay; too low degrades gracefully toward unpaced bursts. Ignored when audio pacing is off.

outputBufferMs.description: Output smoothing buffer (ms). 0 = OFF (lowest latency — keep for SRT/RIST live sources). Raise to absorb bursty sources (e.g. an HLS player that emits at segment boundaries): a non-leaky queue holds up to this much per output and re-feeds it steadily instead of dropping packets mid-frame. Adds this much latency; pick the largest delay you can tolerate for HLS, leave at 0 for low-latency live.
